blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Retail & Consumer Goods, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Demand signals too slow
Batch demand models react to last week; promotions, weather and local events shift baskets daily. Markdown decisions and replenishment both inherit the lag.
Personalization without privacy architecture
Personalization programs stall between marketing ambition and privacy office veto; consent, preference and profiling rules are retrofitted after launch.
Replenishment and allocation by rules of thumb
Store allocation, DC replenishment and size-curve decisions run on legacy heuristics; phantom availability and overstock coexist across the network.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Price-transparency/consumer-protection rules and EU AI Act transparency. Personalization and pricing automation disclosure expectations. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
